Definition: from G5384 and G3581; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.
BiblicalUsage: Philoxenos means hospitable, fond of guests, and it is a mark of the church's leaders and people alike. A bishop must be given to hospitality, an elder must be a lover of hospitality, and all believers are told to use hospitality one to another without grudging.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hospitality without grudging is the test of the open door: the guest is welcomed, the host does not complain, and Christ is honoured in both.
